title: Dragging a node in visual shader editor doesn't auto scroll.
body:
### Tested versions

4.6 dev 5

### System information

Godot v4.6.dev5 - Nobara Linux 43 (Workstation Edition) on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU - Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 9 185H (22 threads) - 62.40 GiB memory

### Issue description

This is an UX inconsistency which I've been told might count as an enhancement.

When you drag a node in the scene tree and approach the top or bottom edge of the area, the tree auto scrolls.

However, if you do the same in the visual shader editor, nothing happens.

I believe that this is a more serious UX issue than in the scene tree because:
1. You often can scroll with the mouse wheel while dragging in a list/tree anyway which doesn't work in a graph.
2. You can have a node graph larger than your current view (even at furthest zoom out) which means that you might not be able to select all the nodes you want.
3. Very often you want to drag a node way outside the current view (even at furthest zoom out) which means you have to drag to the edge, drop, reposition the view, drag again and repeat that several times depending on the size of your graph.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a node in the visual shader editor.
2. Drag it to the edge of the view.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

No need.
